title: Global degree data for a finite Galois extension of a DVR
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$. Let $L/K$ be a finite normal separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], where normal means that every element's minimal polynomial over $K$ splits into linear factors over $L$. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)$ and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The set $X$ of maximal ideals of $B$ is finite and nonempty, and $G$ acts transitively on $X$. For each $\mathfrak q\in X$, the localization $B_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a discrete valuation ring and $A\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is local. For uniformizers $\pi_A$ and $t_{\mathfrak q}$, write $\pi_A=u_{\mathfrak q}t_{\mathfrak q}^{e_{\mathfrak q}}$ with $u_{\mathfrak q}$ a unit, and put $f_{\mathfrak q}=[B/\mathfrak q:k]$, the vector-space degree [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Then $e_{\mathfrak q}$ and $f_{\mathfrak q}$ are finite positive integers independent of $\mathfrak q$. Writing their common values as $e,f$ and $g=|X|$, one has $[L:K]=g e f$.

source.place: Tag 09E8 (remark-finite-separable-extension), the DVR localizations and sum of e_i f_i; Tag 09EA (lemma-galois), transitivity; Tag 09EB (lemma-galois-conclusion), common e,f and [L:K]=nef.

proof.text: By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $A$ is an integral domain in which every ideal is principal. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] applies and gives both that $A$ is Noetherian and that it is a normal domain. By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], its Krull dimension is one.

source.place: Tags 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr) and 00IC (lemma-valuation-ring-normal); preliminary hypotheses of Tag 09E8

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] to the Noetherian normal domain $A$ of Step 1 and the given finite separable extension $L/K$: $B$ is finite over $A$. The integral-closure construction is integral over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $B$ is a domain with fraction field $L$. Apply [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres] to the one-dimensional Noetherian domain $A$ and the finite field extension $L/K$. It gives that $B$ is Dedekind and the map on spectra is surjective, has finite fibres, and induces finite residue field extensions.

source.place: Tag 09E8 (remark-finite-separable-extension), first paragraph; Algebra Tags 032L and 09IG

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-ideal-in-radical] with $I=\mathfrak m_A$, every maximal ideal of the integral $A$-algebra $B$ contracts to the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ of $A$. Conversely, a prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak m_A$ is nonzero, since it contains the nonzero image of a uniformizer of $A$; it is maximal because $B$ is a one-dimensional domain. Thus $X$ is exactly the fibre over $\mathfrak m_A$, which is finite and nonempty by Step 2.

source.place: Tag 09E8, maximal ideals are precisely primes over the base maximal ideal

proof.text: For $\mathfrak q\in X$, [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr] applies to the Dedekind domain $B$ of Step 2 and makes $B_{\mathfrak q}$ a DVR. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak q B_{\mathfrak q}$. The inverse image of this ideal in $A$ is $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$, so $A\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is local. Its residue field is $B/\mathfrak q$: explicitly $b/s\mapsto\bar b/\bar s$ maps onto $B/\mathfrak q$, has kernel $\mathfrak q B_{\mathfrak q}$, and is well-defined since $s\notin\mathfrak q$. The finite residue extension in Step 2 therefore gives finite $f_{\mathfrak q}>0$, the degree of a nonzero field extension.

source.place: Tag 09E8, local DVR extensions and residue degrees; Algebra Tag 034X

proof.text: The image of $\pi_A$ in $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is nonzero (all rings embed in $L$) and lies in its maximal ideal by Step 4. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a local domain whose maximal ideal is $t_{\mathfrak q}B_{\mathfrak q}\neq0$, and every ideal is principal, so it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] applies: the image of $\pi_A$ is $u_{\mathfrak q}t_{\mathfrak q}^{e_{\mathfrak q}}$ with $e_{\mathfrak q}\ge0$. The exponent is positive because exponent zero would make $\pi_A$ a unit. The exponent is unique: if $ut^a=vt^b$ with $a<b$, cancellation in the domain gives the unit $u=vt^{b-a}$ in the maximal ideal, a contradiction. If $t$ and $t′$ generate the same maximal ideal, write $t=at′$ and $t′=bt$; cancellation gives $ab=1$, so $a$ is a unit. Replacing $t$ by $t′$ therefore only changes the unit factor, and uniqueness gives the same exponent.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion; More on Algebra Tag 09E8, ramification indices

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-finite-galois-prime-residue-lifting] with the normal domain $A$ of Step 1 and the given finite normal separable extension. It supplies the restriction action of $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)$ on $B$. For $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak q'\in X$, their contractions are both $\mathfrak m_A$ by Step 3, so the same node supplies $\sigma\in G$ with $\sigma(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q'$. Automorphisms take maximal ideals to maximal ideals; hence this is a transitive action on $X$.

For such $\sigma$, the maps $b/s\mapsto\sigma(b)/\sigma(s)$ and its inverse give an $A$-algebra isomorphism $B_{\mathfrak q}\simeq B_{\mathfrak q'}$. It takes $t_{\mathfrak q}$ to a generator of the target maximal ideal, hence to a unit times $t_{\mathfrak q'}$. Apply it to $\pi_A=u_{\mathfrak q}t_{\mathfrak q}^{e_{\mathfrak q}}$; it fixes $\pi_A$, so the uniqueness proved in Step 5 gives $e_{\mathfrak q}=e_{\mathfrak q'}$. The map $b\bmod\mathfrak q\mapsto\sigma(b)\bmod\mathfrak q'$ gives a $k$-linear field isomorphism $B/\mathfrak q\simeq B/\mathfrak q'$. Mapping a basis through it gives equal dimensions, so $f_{\mathfrak q}=f_{\mathfrak q'}$. Nonemptiness of $X$ now gives common finite positive integers $e,f$.

source.place: Tag 09EB (lemma-galois-conclusion), equality of the indices and degrees spelled out

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-dvr-norm-valuation-sum] to $A\subset B$ with fraction fields $K\subset L$ and $y=\pi_A$. Finiteness of $B/A$, the fraction field, and the finite extension are Step 2 and the hypotheses; the finite set of maximal ideals and their contractions are Step 3; the local DVRs and finite residue degrees are Step 4. Put $n=[L:K]$. Multiplication by $\pi_A$ on an $n$-element $K$-basis of $L$ has diagonal matrix $\pi_A I_n$, so by [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant] $N_{L/K}(\pi_A)=\pi_A^n$. The normalized valuation is the uniformizer exponent, so the left side of the norm formula is $n$ and its summand at $\mathfrak q$ is $f_{\mathfrak q}e_{\mathfrak q}$. Hence $[L:K]=\sum_{\mathfrak q\in X}e_{\mathfrak q}f_{\mathfrak q}$. By Step 7 this is the sum of $g=|X|$ identical terms $ef$, namely $gef$.

Reused finite normalization, Dedekind/fibre, maximal-contraction, DVR-localization and Galois-prime-conjugacy nodes. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N7-9402a1b27 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 8 steps, the new helper and every cited statement, and checked them against Stacks 02MJ (algebra.tex:30038, with its proof and definition-ord), 09E8, 09EA and 09EB (more-algebra.tex), and the blueprint main-20261015 lem-exc-dvr-galois proof, paragraph 1. The item statement matches 09E8/09EB and is unchanged and not weakened. Small cases work: Q(i)/Q over Z_(2), Z_(3) and Z_(5) all give 2=gef. The helper lem-exc-dvr-norm-valuation-sum is a true DVR special case of 02MJ: ord is the normalized valuation, and I tested it on Z_(2)[i] with y=1+i and y=2+i, on units and on inverses. It is strictly more general than the parent, holding for arbitrary y with no Galois hypothesis. It is not elementary, has no duplicate in the DAG (rg for 02MJ, 09E8, sum_ramification_inertia and norm/valuation statements) and is not a Mathlib one-liner, so unsplit is correct. I checked every step's hypotheses: 032L Noetherian+normal+separable, 09IG one-dimensional Noetherian, the radical node with I=m_A, Dedekind localization, conjugacy from the 0BRK leaf, and the elementary e/f transport by sigma. The tool_use lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres is accepted as a generic Krull-Akizuki black box. Two repairable citation faults are fixed in fixes/: (B3/C1) the helper statement and item step 8 used the field-norm determinant without a node, and both now cite def-weil-endomorphism-determinant; (C4) item step 5 applied the unit-times-uniformizer-power node, which needs Noetherian, without citing where that comes from, and it now cites def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring and lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal. proof_deps was recomputed.
